text: The assembly will now hear an address by
her excellency Ko Sophia Fujimori
Higuchi, President of the Republic of
Peru. I request protocol to escort her
excellency and invite her to address the
assembly.
President,
>> President of the General Assembly,
Secretary General,
Ladies and gentlemen, heads of state and
government,
distinguished delegates,
I
am taking the floor to address you at
this global rostrm,
bringing the greetings to you of an
age-old civilization. We have
civilizations that date back more than
5,000 years. I come from a land in which
history
was carved into stone and in which
geographical challenges
were transformed into opportunities for
civilizations to meet. Centuries ago,
the Incor
built Kapakan,
a majestic network of roads that was
built
to
meet the peoples,
to bring together diverse realities
and to ensure that no corner of the
empire was left isolated and forgotten.
This same spirit,
this spirit that seeks to bring together
is the spirit that brings us here today.
I am appearing at the General Assembly
of the United Nations. Today for the
first time,
only 57 days ago, I had the honor of
assuming the presidency of the Republic
of Peru.
Mine is a proud and resilient people and
we are a founding member state of this
organization.
Peru
comes to this assembly
reaffirming its ironclad commitment to
the United Nations Charter and its
fundamental principles, peace and
security, development and human rights,
the three pillars of the United Nations.
I come from a country
which is all too well aware of the high
price of peace. We conquered terrorism.
But regrettably today still after 34
years.
Those who took up that mantle continue
to be judged and tried despite the fact
that they have demonstrated that due
process was violated.
Peru as other Latin American countries
has
seen agendas imposed upon us that have
divided us as a as a society. Politics
have been instrumentalized.
Democracy has been eros eroded and the
institution of the family has been
weakened. An institution that is so
crucial for the Peruvian people.
The United Nations
must continue to stand as the meeting
place excellence for our peoples. A
meeting place which respects diverse
realities and traditions
always within the framework of peace,
development and human rights.
Consequently,
we express our hope
that we will
seek to rebuild trust and we hope that
in that endeavor the United Nations will
act independently impartially and show
that it has a true vocation for
dialogue. The United Nations must show
us that it can forge paths including
and even when understanding seems
impossible to achieve, let us seek to
grow stronger and
fly the flag of the very reset of this
organization. That is to find common
ground on common issues, including when
we hold different opinions.
After more than three decades in my
country's policies, I can bear witness
to how the Peruvian people have endured
periods or rather experienced periods of
intense hope in which trust in
democrating institutions and governments
has actually grown stronger. We have
forged ahead because in addition to
defeating terrorism, we have proven able
to almost triple in real terms
our GDP.
We have multiplied 15fold the value of
our exports and we have ensured that our
currency is now among the most stable in
the world.
Despite this progress, the most recent
governments were not capable of
addressing new challenges or of closing
the social divides which continue to
remain in Peru. We continue to have
structural problems that need to be
resolved. problems that styy more
uniform development, divides and
problems which erode citizens trusts in
democratic institutions and authorities.
Allow me to share with you ladies and
gentlemen some of the most pressing
challenges that Peru is currently
facing. The first major challenge we
face is the frontal assault we must wage
on organized crime and petty crime. Peru
is located on a continent in which there
are no wars between nations.
However, we are faced with another type
of war that is that declared by
transnational criminal organizations.
organizations that have sowed terror
among our people.
In this war, there are no battle
grounds, no fronts. Indeed, no fronts
have been defined. There are no
international rules governing these
conflicts. The enemy does not wear a
uniform. The enemy hides among our
people.
There is no possibility
to see surrender or to sign peace
treaties. In this context,
confronting this war as an isolated
problem to be dealt with by each nation
alone is not only mistaken thinking and
a mistake that we've been making.
Rather, it is an act of giving the
advantage to transnational organized
crime. to make that mistake allows them
to grow stronger. They have huge
economic and wararmongering power and
they get that through crimes and illegal
businesses that re range from smuggling,
illegal mining, drug trafficking, human
trafficking, extortion and killing.
Consequently, the first thing we must do
is isolate or pinpoint and identify the
enemy. These organizations, these
enemies are terrorist groups and they
must be tackled for as what they are.
They are enemies of a democratic state
and of fine upstanding citizens.
Clearly defining
what who the enemy is and establishing a
normative framework will allow the armed
forces in supporting the national police
to act with resolve and tackle the
threat to the domestic order posed by
these organizations.
Moreover,
in addition to actively participating
in the regional Santiago Pact,
Peru recently joined the Shield of the
Americas. That was a demonstration of
its decisive commitment to working
together and in concert with our
partners
in
this challenge which is of the utmost
priority for Peru. In Peru, we will
pursue crime and prosecute it. We'll go
after the man that commits the crimes
and go after the network that supports
him. We will not waver in the face of
those that attempt to impose terror over
and above the law.
Suppressing, repressing these
organizations
will do that with the full force of the
law. But doing that is not enough
if at the same time we do not tackle the
challenge that is developing a better
educational system.
There need to be effective opportunities
for learning for our children and young
people. It's only through providing
those that young people and adults can
enter the labor markets
instead of being recruited by criminal
groups. Consequently, our second
challenge will be that of making
education a tool for social
transformation and a tool for the
prevention of violence and crime.
The quality of education
and the depth of learning enjoyed by our
children and young people is a predictor
of higher a higher quality of life
because such education make it possible
to develop higher income better health
habits and that serves the cause of
social mobility.
On the other hand, we've noted that
shortcomings and weak points in our
education system combine with other
factors to predict crime and indeed fuel
crime.
With that in mind, my government has
launched a wholesale reform of the
Peruvian education system. This reform
will strengthen educational
infrastructure. It will increase the
provision of digital learning and the
provision of educational material. We
will also bolster
the resources given to teachers to
teach. At the heart of our reform will
be the creation of a headteer training
school. The goal is to equip head
teachers with the tools and skills they
need
to lead their schools independently
so that schools can become inspiring
models that promote the participation of
parents in this mission that is that of
making every child a a citizen that
stands in solidarity with others,
respects them and a citizen proud of
their country.
I must recognize that an ideological
cultural agenda that is not in line with
our reality and the imposition of it has
sowed confusion and disorder of such
magnitude that today teachers in our
schools are not able to keep order in
the classroom.
They cannot discipline their classes
because they cower under the threat of
being reported. We need to reestablish
the principle of respect for authority.
We will make our classrooms safe spaces
in which children go to learn
and teachers go to teach without fear.
This is our agenda. It is not that of
anyone else being imposed. The role of a
state is to withdraw unfair barriers.
Barriers that styy p people's
development. We intend to provide people
with the conditions they need to thrive.
Effort, talent, and freedom as shown by
everybody should then do the rest. Our
third major challenge is that of
strengthening our institutions and our
democracy. In Peru, we believe in the
freedom of individuals. We believe in
the family as an irreplaceable pillar of
our society. We believe in respecting
tradition.
We believe in equality before the law
and human dignity.
And of course we believe in the new name
of peace that is justice. The fact is
that in our quest to ensure that freedom
can be fully exercised by all we have to
underscore the overriding need for a
judiciary which imposes the law in full
respect of due process and individual
freedoms.
Consequently, Peru is of the view that
genuine democracy is achieved with
respect for the independence and
autonomy of powers,
firm justice, ironclad justice, which is
truly impartial and committed to due
process.
The defense of human rights must not
ultimately turn victims into those in
the dock and
torturers into those we protect. The
rights of citizens
must must begin when impunity of the
torturer comes to an end. As such, it is
up to the international community to act
with the same resolve in the face of any
and all violations when we are at our
most vulnerable.
Peruvians don't always find a place
within the international community or
the empathy that they need or or loyalty
to the principles that gave rise to this
general assembly. The fact is that the
international community
really acquires true logic and meaning
when it manages to be present at the
most critical difficult junctures.
The international community must act
within its own limits and ensure there
is a community of sovereign nations.
Supporting a country does not mean
replacing its institutions or overriding
the decisions that it is up to its
citizens to make within the democratic
order.
We can share universal principles and at
the same time recognize that every
people has its own story, its own
history, its own culture, its own
traditions and the legitimate right to
democratically
define its own path.
We hope to see independent,
transparent action which does not make
ideological calculations and without
those calculations manages to respect
and ensure all human rights, the rights
of peasants, children, women, the rights
of police forces and members of the
military that are on the front line in
the defense of life and freedom. This
forum has before it the historic duty to
be a space for the meeting, the coming
together of equals, a place for genuine
cooperation free of external dictats and
attempts to standardize and homogenize
thought. Those of us that come from
nations that are constantly having to
recover and get back on their feet, we
come here today absolutely sure of the
fact that we can share great principles
without ever turning our back on what we
are. We do not need to all think in the
same way to have deep mutual respect for
one another. The world does not require
identical democracies. It requires
legitimate democracies.
It does not demand nations that are all
the same. It does not need cookie cutter
nations. It means needs truly free
peoples. Thank you.
On behalf of the assembly, I wish to
thank the president of the Republic of
Peru.
